topic: Indeterminate structures: slope deflection method and moment distribution method, use of influence line diagrams for simple beams, unit load method, two hinged arch
source: structure 1-70 / 71-140 / 141-228 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 111. A statically indeterminate structure is the one which
options: cannot be analysed using the equations of statics alone
is not stable for general loading
can be analysed with the equations of statics alone
questions.explain: Statically indeterminate structures have more unknowns than available equilibrium equations and require compatibility equations for analysis.

questions.q: 119. The statically indeterminate structure can be solved by
options: ignoring all deformations and assuming the structure to be rigid
using the equations of statics and the necessary number of equations of compatibility
questions.explain: Indeterminate structures require both equilibrium equations (statics) and displacement-based equations (compatibility) to be fully solved.

questions.q: 120. The equations of compatibility are written based on
options: the geometry of the deformed structure under the action of several forces acting
questions.explain: Compatibility equations ensure that the deformed shape of the structure is geometrically continuous and consistent with the supports.

questions.q: 125. An externally indeterminate structure is the one in which
options: the total number of external reaction components is more than the equations of statics applicable to the structure as a whole
the total number of external reaction components is more than the degree of indeterminacy
the sum of external reaction components and the degree of internal redundancy is greater than three
questions.explain: External indeterminacy occurs when the number of support reactions exceeds the available static equilibrium equations.

questions.q: 126. An internally indeterminate structure
options: may be an unstable structure based on supports
questions.explain: Internal indeterminacy refers to the redundancy of internal members; per the provided key, it is categorized here relative to an externally determinate setup.

questions.q: 127. A frame is completely analysed, when
options: the variation in shear is found throughout the frame
the variation in direct stress, shear and moment is found throughout the frame
the shear and moment reaction from member to member are known at every joint
questions.explain: Complete analysis of a frame requires determining all internal actions, including axial (direct) stress, shear force, and bending moments across all members.

questions.q: 128. A prop is
options: An additional support provided to a stable structure to avoid any displacement at the desired point in a direction perpendicular to the plane of the prop
the support which gives the maximum number of reactions for the stability of the structure
a support which will not affect the geometry of the deformed structure
a dummy support provided for architectural purposes
questions.explain: A prop is a redundant support (often a roller or hinge) added to a structure to reduce deflection or provide extra stability at a specific point.

questions.q: 129. A rigid prop is one which
options: permits 50% of free deflection, that would have occurred if the prop were not there
does not permit any displacement perpendicular to that plane of prop
supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
questions.explain: A rigid prop acts as an unyielding support, meaning the vertical displacement (deflection) at the point of the prop is forced to be zero.

questions.q: 130. An elastic prop is one which
options: supports the entire load and relieves all other supports completely
develops reaction proportional to the compression in itself
questions.explain: An elastic prop (like a spring) provides a reaction force that is proportional to its deformation, following Hooke's Law (F = kx).

questions.q: 131. A sinking prop is one which
options: does not permit any deflection at all
is provided below the level of regular supports and becomes effective after the respective deflection occurs
questions.explain: A sinking prop refers to a support that undergoes a predetermined settlement or only engages once the structure has deflected to a certain point.

questions.q: 138. Find the DSI of propped cantilever beam
questions.explain: A propped cantilever has 4 reaction components (3 at fixed end + 1 at prop). With 3 equilibrium equations, the Degree of Static Indeterminacy (DSI) is 4 - 3 = 1.

questions.q: 139. DSI of structure depends upon
questions.explain: DSI is a geometric property determined by the arrangement of members and the types of joints (rigid vs. pinned) and supports.

questions.q: 140. The ends of continuous beam should be
questions.explain: The end of a continuous beam can be configured in various ways—fixed, pinned, roller, or cantilever—depending on the design requirements.

questions.q: 144. If the co moment of Joint A, B, & C are 10, 20 and 30 kN-m then find the balancing moment at joint B.
questions.explain: In the Moment Distribution Method, the balancing moment is equal in magnitude but opposite in sign to the out-of-balance moment at the joint to maintain equilibrium.

questions.q: 146. The theorem of three moments for the solution of continuous beams is formulated by
questions.explain: Clapeyron's Theorem of Three Moments is a relationship between the bending moments at three consecutive supports of a continuous beam.

questions.q: 148. The moment distribution method is formulated by
questions.explain: Hardy Cross published the Moment Distribution Method in 1930, providing a simple iterative way to analyze indeterminate structures.

questions.q: 149. The simultaneous equations of slope deflection method can be solved by iteration in
questions.explain: The Moment Distribution Method is essentially an iterative procedure for solving the same equations found in the slope-deflection method.

questions.q: 150. Slope deflection method is
questions.explain: The Slope Deflection method is a displacement (deflection) method of structural analysis that relates end moments to joint rotations and displacements.

questions.q: 151. Moment distribution method is
questions.explain: The Moment Distribution Method (Hardy Cross method) is an iterative process; it is fundamentally an approximation technique used to solve for bending moments without solving simultaneous equations.

questions.q: 152. Degree of freedom (DOF) or DKI, for the structure is
questions.explain: Based on the standard analysis of the joint configuration shown in typical structural problems of this level, the kinematic indeterminacy (DKI) is 2.

questions.q: 153. The stiffness factor at the near end of a member with far end hinged is
questions.explain: When the far end is hinged (pinned), the moment required to produce unit rotation at the near end is 3EI/L. If the far end were fixed, it would be 4EI/L.

questions.q: 154. The ratio of stiffness of a member when far end is hinged to that of the member when far end is fixed is
questions.explain: The ratio is (3EI/L) / (4EI/L) = 3/4. This is a common factor used in the Moment Distribution Method to adjust stiffness for pinned supports.

questions.q: 155. At a joint where several members meet, any applied moment will be distributed among the various members
options: equally among such members whose far ends are fixed
equally among such members whose far ends are hinged
questions.explain: According to the principle of moment distribution, an applied moment is shared by members meeting at a joint in direct proportion to their relative stiffness (K).

questions.q: 156. The distribution factor of a member at a joint is
options: the ratio of the moment borne by the member to the total moment applied at the joint
the ratio of the area of the member to the sum of the areas of several members
the ratio of the moment induced at the far end to the moment applied at the near end
equally among such members whose far ends are hinged
questions.explain: The Distribution Factor (DF) is defined as the ratio of the stiffness of a particular member to the total stiffness of all members meeting at that joint.

questions.q: 157. If ki is the stiffness of i th member of a Joint, the distribution factor for the member is
questions.explain: Mathematically, the DF for a member 'i' is expressed as the stiffness of that member divided by the sum of the stiffnesses of all members at the joint: DF = Ki / ΣKi.

questions.q: 161. In hingeless arch, it is supposed to
questions.explain: A hingeless (fixed) arch is statically indeterminate; per the provided key, it refers to specific constraints or a 2nd-degree analysis found in certain textbook contexts.

questions.q: 162. If there is a cantilever beam joined with the edge of the span, then it is
questions.explain: Joining a cantilever to an existing span introduces additional redundant constraints or internal forces that cannot be solved by simple static equilibrium equations alone, making the structure indeterminate.

questions.q: 163. Influence line is
options: the line showing stress function due to unit moving load
the line showing stress function due to unit load
the line showing stress function due to udl
questions.explain: By definition, an Influence Line Diagram (ILD) represents the variation of a specific response (stress function like shear, moment, or reaction) at a fixed section as a unit load moves across the structure.

questions.q: 164. The line showing the variations of stress function at a given point due to a unit load moving on a span is known as
questions.explain: This is the formal definition of an influence line; it tracks how a single 'unit' load affects one specific point as that load changes position.

questions.q: 165. Influence lines are drawn for structures
questions.explain: Influence lines are a universal tool in structural engineering, used for both determinate (linear) and indeterminate (typically curved) structures.

questions.q: 166. Which one is right w.r.t. ILD?
options: it is the BMD due to unit load
it is the BMD due to static unit load
it is the BMD due to moving unit load
it is the BMD due to impacting unit load
questions.explain: The ILD specifically captures the effects of a moving unit load, unlike a standard BMD which shows the effect of a fixed load along the whole beam.

questions.q: 167. The influence line diagram for S.F. or BM at a section is
options: the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section when the unit load is placed over that section only
the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section when the unit load is at the centre of the span
the variation in the value of S.F. or B.M. at that section as the unit load transverses the span from left to right
questions.explain: An ILD for a section must show the full range of variation (the 'influence') as the unit load moves from the start of the span to the end.

questions.q: 168. The influence line diagram for reaction at a support of a simply supported beam is
options: a triangle with ordinate 1 at that support
a triangle with ordinate 1 at the other support
questions.explain: For a support reaction RA, the reaction is 1 when the unit load is exactly at A, and 0 when it is at the other support B, creating a right-angled triangle with a peak (ordinate) of 1 at support A.

questions.q: 169. The influence line diagram for reaction at the support of a cantilever will be a
options: triangle with zero ordinate at fixed end and unit ordinate at free end
triangle with unit ordinate at fixed end and zero ordinate at free end
questions.explain: In a cantilever, any vertical load placed anywhere on the beam must be fully resisted by the single vertical reaction at the fixed support. Therefore, the reaction is always 1, resulting in a rectangle with unit ordinate.

questions.q: 170. The influence line diagram for shear force at a section on a cantilever will be
options: a rectangle of length equal to full length of span with unit ordinate
a rectangle extending between free end and the section with unit ordinate
a triangle extending for whole length of span with unit ordinate at fixed support
a triangle extending between the section and the fixed end with unit ordinate at fixed support
questions.explain: Shear force at a section in a cantilever only exists when the load is between the free end and that section, creating a rectangle from the section to the free end.

questions.q: 171. The influence line diagram for BM at a section in a cantilever will be a triangle extending between the section and the
options: fixed end with maximum ordinate under the section
fixed end with maximum ordinate under the fixed end
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the section
unsupported end with maximum ordinate at the supported end
questions.explain: The bending moment at a section is created by the load multiplied by its distance from that section. The maximum moment occurs when the unit load is at the farthest possible point from the support (the free/unsupported end).

questions.q: 172. The influence line diagram for BM at a section of a simply supported beam will be a
options: triangle with maximum ordinate at the section and zero at the two supports
triangle with maximum ordinate at the support nearer to the section and zero at the other support
questions.explain: For a simply supported beam, the B.M. at a section 'C' is zero when the load is at either support and reaches its maximum value (ab/L) when the load is directly on the section.

questions.q: 188. Which of the following methods of structure analysis is a force method?
questions.explain: Column Analogy and Method of Consistent Deformation are Force Methods (Flexibility Methods), where redundant forces are the unknowns. Slope Deflection and Moment Distribution are Displacement Methods.

questions.q: 194. Degree of static indeterminacy of the frame is equal to
questions.explain: Calculated using Ds = 3c - r', where 'c' is the number of closed loops and 'r' represents the releases at supports or hinges.

questions.q: 198. Portal method of framed analysis for horizontal loads is appropriate for a frame:
options: that has a width greater than its height
that has a height greater than its width
questions.explain: The portal method is an approximate method suitable for low-rise frames where the width is significant relative to the height.

questions.q: 206. Which of the following structural analysis is a force method?
questions.explain: Column analogy treats the redundants as forces, making it a force-based method.

questions.q: 207. Stiffness factor is calculated in structural members for analyzing it by
questions.explain: The moment distribution method relies heavily on member stiffness to distribute unbalanced moments.

questions.q: 211. Unequal settlement in the supports of statically indeterminate structure develop
questions.explain: Settlement in indeterminate structures induces internal forces and reactions that wouldn't exist in a determinate structure.

questions.q: 212. In approximate analysis of building frames under lateral loads, the point of contraflexure in columns is assumed at
questions.explain: Methods like the Portal and Cantilever methods assume the point of zero moment (contraflexure) is at the mid-height of the column.

questions.q: 213. The moment distribution method is best suited for
questions.explain: MDM is specifically designed for rigid frames and continuous beams where joint rotations occur.

questions.q: 214. In the moment distribution method, the sum of distribution factors of all the members meeting at any joint is always :
questions.explain: The total unbalanced moment must be 100% distributed, so ΣDF = 1.

questions.q: 215. The stiffness method in structural analysis is also known as :
questions.explain: The stiffness method uses displacements as the primary unknowns, hence it is a displacement method.
